original_question: Has the protein encoded by the gene associated with Hay-Wells syndrome been observed to be overexpressed in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma?

final_qi.question: Has the protein encoded by the gene associated with Hay-Wells syndrome been observed to be overexpressed in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma?
final_qi.long_answer: Hay-Wells (AEC) syndrome is caused by heterozygous mutations in the TP63 gene, which encodes the p63 transcription factor. Immunohistochemical and molecular studies of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) consistently report strong, diffuse nuclear p63 staining in the vast majority of tumors, whereas normal vulvar epithelium shows p63 mainly restricted to the basal/parabasal layers. This wider and more intense expression is interpreted as over-expression of the TP63-encoded protein in VSCC. Therefore, the protein encoded by the Hay-Wells–associated gene has indeed been observed to be overexpressed in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma.
